_about:
Source of data/archetypes.json. Edit here, then run: python3 tools/build_archetypes.py

Each archetype generalises a pattern seen in several real works (see `basis`). Slots in templates:
  {m1} {m2} {m3}   materials picked for this work (m1 is the main one)
  {count} {count_word} {n} {months} {minutes} {year_then} {hours}
  {place}          the artist's home city      {heritage}  the practice or history the artist draws on
  {phrase}         a short phrase from lexicon  {colour}    a colour
  {region_word}    e.g. "the north"            {unit}      archetype-specific unit noun

scenes: {count_word} hand-sewn patchwork banners hang from the roof trusses at different heights, each carrying a short phrase in capital letters cut from {m2}.
Long banners of {m1} and {m2} hang in rows from a steel grid, so that visitors walk between them as between laundry lines. Each banner is stitched with a phrase in the artist's mother tongue.
facts: The {m1} came from {count} households in {place}, collected by the artist over {months} months.
The phrases were gathered in workshops with {n} residents of {place}, who were asked what they would say to their grandchildren.
Some of the banners were first carried in a procession through {place} in {year_then}.
process: Each banner was cut and stitched by hand in the artist's studio with a group of {n} women.
The letters were cut from {m2} and sewn on with a running stitch the artist learned from {heritage}.
quotes: I wanted words that you could wear, and wash, and give to someone else.
A banner is a sentence that needs a crowd to finish it.
turns: Hung high above the visitor and moving with every draught, the phrases read less as slogans than as a chorus that has not yet agreed on its words.
Read together, the banners suggest that a crowd can be stitched as well as gathered.
archetypes.camera: wide view along the hall at eye level, the banners receding in perspective

scenes: A vast lattice woven from {m1} stretches overhead across the first room, forming a canopy that throws a net of shadows onto the floor and walls.
A woven structure of {m1} and {m2} hangs from the ceiling in {count} loose parts, so that visitors can walk in and out of it as through a curtain.

core: aluminium bottle seals and copper wire

facts: The weave follows a pattern used for sleeping mats in {place}, scaled up {count} times.
It took {n} weavers {months} months to complete, working in shifts in a rented warehouse.
process: The structure was woven on site over {hours} days, knot by knot, without a drawing.
Every knot is tied by hand; the artist describes the process as counting without numbers.
quotes: A mat is the first architecture. You are born on it and you are laid out on it.
We wanted to make a shelter you can see through.
turns: Overhead and porous, the canopy offers shelter without walls, a roof that holds the visitor without enclosing them.
The shadows it casts change with the light outside, so that the work is never finished being woven.
archetypes.camera: low angle from the floor looking up into the canopy, the room's roof visible behind

scenes: Tall sheets of {m1}, dyed in the warm tones of {m2}, hang in a line through the room. Each is torn and then carefully darned, the newest tears still open.
A single length of {m1} hangs from the ceiling under one spotlight, its tail trailing across the floor like a train. The cloth is stained in uneven bands of {colour}.
facts: Each of the {count} tears marks a site in {place} that was damaged or demolished since {year_then}.
The cloth was soaked for {n} days in water collected from {count} neighbourhoods of {place}.
process: The darning was done by hand over {months} months, one tear at a time.
The dyes were boiled in the artist's kitchen from plants with known healing uses.
quotes: Mending is slower than destroying. That is the only argument I have.
I am not repairing the cloth. I am keeping it company.
turns: The stitches do not hide the damage; they make it the most carefully made part of the work.
The fabric holds the city in its stains, a map that can only be read by touch.
archetypes.camera: frontal view down the line of hanging sheets, soft side light

scenes: A very wide embroidered hanging, almost {w_m} metres long, runs along the wall like a mural. It is crowded with small scenes of daily life in {place}: weddings, a market, a flood, a funeral.
{count_word} embroidered panels hang edge to edge, each made by a different woman from {place}, together forming a patchwork map of the town.
facts: The hanging was made by {n} members of a women's embroidery group founded in {place} in {year_then}.
Each scene was drawn from a story told during weekly meetings over {months} months.
process: The women stitched in pairs, passing the cloth between houses.
Nothing was drawn in advance; each woman embroidered what she remembered.
quotes: We sewed what the newspapers did not print.
The needle is how we take minutes.
turns: What looks like decoration from a distance turns out, up close, to be a record kept by people who were never asked to keep one.
The work proposes the sewing circle as a kind of archive, slower and more crowded than any other.
archetypes.camera: frontal view of the long hanging on a white wall, the floor and a bench visible

scenes: Long strands of {m1}, dyed in {colour} and knotted at the top, hang from the ceiling to the floor in a dense forest that stirs as visitors pass.
Hundreds of knotted cords of {m1} and {m2} hang in rows from a ring suspended over the room, brushing the floor.
facts: The knots follow the logic of the khipu, the knotted cords used in the Andes to record numbers and, some say, stories.
The wool came from {n} flocks in the hills above {place}.
process: Each cord was knotted by the artist while listening to recordings of {heritage}.
The strands were dyed in {count} baths, so that no two are the same colour.
quotes: A knot is a word that cannot be erased.
I make a space where the thread can speak.
turns: The cords move with the breath of the visitors, as if the record were still being written.
archetypes.camera: looking through the hanging strands towards the far wall, soft daylight

scenes: {count_word} ceremonial garments made of {m1} hang empty at head height from a rail, facing the door as if waiting for wearers.
A row of {count_word} costumes covered in {m2} stands on low plinths, their sleeves sewn shut.
facts: The garments are modelled on the dress worn for {heritage}, which the artist's family stopped making in {year_then}.
They were worn once, in a performance through {place} on the night before the exhibition opened.
process: Each garment took about {months} months to bead.
The patterns were copied from photographs in a museum storeroom the artist was allowed to visit for {n} days.
quotes: Clothes remember a body better than a photograph does.
These are made to be danced in, and the museum will not let anyone dance in them.
turns: Empty and lit like relics, the garments make absence the main performer.
archetypes.camera: frontal medium-wide view of the row of garments against a white wall

scenes: {count_word} life-size figures of rough {m1} stand in a circle, turned inward, their hollow eyes lifted. They are dressed in {m2} and hold small found objects.
A group of {count_word} hand-built {m1} figures, each about a metre high, stands on the floor without plinths, some leaning on each other.
facts: The clay was dug from the riverbank near {place}, where the artist's grandmother made pots for {n} years.
The figures were fired in an open pit, the way pots are still fired in {place}.
process: Each figure was coiled by hand over {months} weeks; the cracks from firing were left as they were.
The artist worked alongside {n} potters from {place} during a residency in {year_then}.
quotes: They are ancestors, and they are also the ones who come after us.
I make bodies that can stand up for themselves.
turns: Facing each other rather than the visitor, the figures make the viewer an outsider to a conversation that was already under way.
archetypes.camera: wide view of the circle from slightly above eye level, the room around it

basis: Emilie Louise Gossiaux, Kong Play, Whitney 2026
scenes: {count_word} small hand-built {m1} vessels stand in precise rows on the floor, some cracked, some holding a little {m2}.

scenes.t: A low two-tiered plinth carries {count_word} {m1} copies of an ordinary household object, each glazed a different colour.

facts: The clay was taken from {count} construction sites around {place}.
There is one vessel for every day the artist spent away from {place} in {year_then}.
process: Each vessel was pinched by hand in a single sitting.
The artist made {n} of them each morning before speaking to anyone.
quotes: A pot is a promise that something will be kept.
Repetition is how my mother prayed.
turns: Seen together, the vessels stop being objects and become a measure of time spent waiting.
archetypes.camera: low view across the rows of vessels on the floor, the far wall softly lit

scenes.t: Clay instruments, from ocarinas to drums, lie on a long plywood table. A handwritten sign invites visitors to play them; a speaker nearby plays a recording of {n} people playing at once.
{count_word} ceramic bells of different sizes hang from a timber frame and are struck at intervals by small motors.

facts: The instruments were made in a village in the region of {place} where {count} roof-tile factories still operate.
The recording was made at a festival in {year_then} where {n} people played together.
process: Each instrument was tuned by ear before firing.
Visitors are encouraged to play; broken pieces are replaced every week.
quotes: The clay already knows the song. We just give it a mouth.
Everyone can play. That is the point.
turns: The work is complete only when it is noisy.
interaction: Visitors are invited to play the instruments.
archetypes.camera: three-quarter view of the long table with instruments, a few chairs around

basis: Berlin Biennale 13 (dirt in a plywood box)
Ersan Mondtag and Yael Bartana, German Pavilion 2024

scenes.t: A plywood box, {h_small} centimetres high, sits on the floor, filled to the brim with dark soil carried from {place}.
A low rectangle of compacted {m1} covers most of the floor. A narrow path of planks crosses it.

facts: The soil was brought from a field outside {place} that the artist's family farmed until {year_then}.
It travelled {n} kilometres by bus, in {count} suitcases.
process: The soil is watered each morning by an invigilator.
At the end of the exhibition the soil will be returned to the field.
quotes: I could not bring my grandmother, so I brought what she stood on.
Soil is the only archive that grows.
turns: A box of earth stands in for a place that cannot travel, and for the people who had to.
change: Over the months of the exhibition, weeds and seeds hidden in the soil begin to sprout.
archetypes.camera: eye-level view of the box in an otherwise empty room

basis: Otobong Nkanga, Central Pavilion facade, Venice 2026
Nhà Sàn Collective garden, documenta fifteen

scenes.t: The columns of the room have been bricked up with {m1}; plants from {place} grow out of the mortar and will, by the end of the exhibition, cover them.
A spiral path of moss-covered earth winds past slowly browning trees and a pond. Mist rises from jets set into the ground.

facts: The {count} plant species were chosen with a botanist in {place}; all of them grow in the gardens of enslaved people's descendants.
0|The bricks were made by hand in {place} from earth mixed with straw.
1|The trees were brought in from a nursery near {place} and will be replanted.
process: The garden is tended every day by a gardener hired for the duration of the exhibition.
Nothing was planted in rows.
quotes: A garden is a slow riot.
I wanted the building to have a body that could change its mind.
change: 0|The vines will slowly climb and obscure the building as the months pass.
1|The trees will brown over the months, and the pond will turn green.
turns: The work will look its best on the day the exhibition closes.
archetypes.camera: wide view, daylight, the plants in the foreground

scenes: A block of {m1} the size of a small car stands in front of a sunlit window. Inside it, as if frozen in a river, hang {m2}, {m3} and scraps of paper.

scenes.t: {count_word} large containers cast in translucent {m1} stand in a row like funerary jars, glowing in the daylight.

facts: 0|The resin was tapped from trees on a plantation outside {place} that has been worked since {year_then}.
0|The documents inside are copies of {count} residence permits from the artist's family.
1|The jars copy the containers used to store water in {place} during a drought in {year_then}.
process: 0|The block was cast in layers over {months} weeks.
0|Heat from the window slowly softens the surface, and it is allowed to crack.
1|The fibreglass was cast in a boatyard.
quotes: I wanted something that remembers by changing.
0|Everything inside is something my mother kept.
1|Water is the first thing a family stores and the last thing it gives away.
change: 0|Warmth from the sun slowly softens, cracks and shifts the block during the exhibition.
turns: 0|As the surface softens and cracks, memory appears less as something stored than as something that moves through the body.
1|Monumental and empty, the jars make scarcity look sacred.
archetypes.camera: frontal view of the block against the bright window, slight silhouette

basis: Marlene Almeida, Terra Viva, São Paulo 2025

scenes.t: Glass vitrines hold pressed plants, jars of {m1}, handwritten labels and a small lead cast of an extinct bird, arranged like a natural history collection.
Shelves of jars containing soils and pigments from {count} sites around {place} line the wall, beside a desk with laboratory glassware and handwritten notes.

facts: 0|The {count} specimens were collected on the edges of a sugar plantation outside {place}.
Several of the plants were used by enslaved women as medicine and are now listed as weeds.
1|The samples come from {count} sites, each marked on a hand-drawn map.
process: Each specimen was pressed and labelled by hand, in both the colonial botanical name and the local one.
The artist worked with a herbalist from {place} over {months} months.
quotes: A weed is a plant whose story nobody wrote down.
I am collecting the plants the botanists left behind.
turns: Borrowing the furniture of the natural history museum, the work fills it with what that museum chose not to keep.
archetypes.camera: close three-quarter view of vitrines and shelves, even museum light

basis: Bagus Pandega and Kei Imazu, Bangkok 2024

scenes.t: Mangrove saplings are slowly raised and lowered by a machine into a tank of water, imitating the tide.
Rotting fruit on polished wooden tables is wired by electrodes to speakers and small lights, which hum and flicker as the fruit decays.

facts: 0|The tidal cycle follows the tide table for {place} on the day the artist was born.
1|The fruit is replaced every {n} days from a market in the city.
1|The fruit comes from a market in {place} that sells what supermarkets refuse.
process: The machine was built with an engineer and runs on a timer.
Nothing is fixed when it breaks; the repairs become part of the work.
0|The machine was built with an engineer and runs on a timer.
quotes: 0|The plant does not need me. I need the plant.
1|Everything here is slowly leaking.
turns: The work stages care as a mechanical routine, and then lets the routine fail.
archetypes.camera: three-quarter view of the apparatus, natural light

scenes: Tables and vitrines hold photocopied documents, some redacted with black marker, alongside family photographs, a rubber stamp and a stack of identity cards. A wall text in {count} languages runs above.
A room-sized display works like a small history museum: photographs, objects, dolls and newspaper cuttings, each with a typed caption, cover the walls from floor to ceiling.
facts: The documents come from a municipal archive in {place} that was opened to the public in {year_then}.
Of the {n} files the artist requested, {count} were released, most of them partly redacted.
process: The artist copied each document by hand before photocopying it.
Captions were written with a retired archivist from {place}.
quotes: The archive is not missing things. It was built to miss them.
I am not adding anything. I am only rearranging what they kept.
turns: The display borrows the authority of the museum to show how authority was used to forget.
archetypes.camera: wide view of the room with tables and walls covered in documents, flat light

scenes: A long table holds photocopied zines and pamphlets, with plastic chairs, a kettle, a shelf of donated books and a handwritten sign that reads FREE.
A room is furnished like an improvised living room, with a sofa, rugs from {place}, a bookshelf and a small television playing a recorded meeting.
facts: The books were donated by {n} members of an artist-run space founded in {place} in {year_then}.
Since it opened, the room has hosted {count} reading groups and one wedding.
process: The furniture was borrowed from the homes of the collective's members.
Visitors may take any publication; the shelves are restocked every week.
quotes: We did not have a school, so we became one.
Nothing here is for sale. Everything here can be taken.
turns: The room turns the exhibition into a place to stay rather than a place to pass through.
interaction: Visitors may sit, read and take publications.
archetypes.camera: eye-level view of the table and shelves, a chair pulled out

scenes.t: A whole wall is covered edge to edge with about {count} small colour prints, pinned in rows like the warp and weft of a textile.
{count_word} small black-and-white photographs hang in a single row at eye level, each showing one person from {place} in front of the same wall.

facts: The photographs were taken over {months} months in {place}, mostly by the people who appear in them.
The oldest picture dates from {year_then}.
process: The prints were hung by the artist alone over {hours} days.
No picture is captioned; a list of names is available at the desk.
quotes: I did not want a single image to speak for everyone.
The camera was passed around like a cigarette.
turns: The sheer number of images makes the ordinary feel monumental, and the monumental feel ordinary.
archetypes.camera: frontal view of the wall of photographs, a visitor in front for scale

basis: Archie Moore, kith and kin, Venice 2024
scenes: The walls and ceiling of a black-painted room are covered by hand in white chalk with a family tree reaching back {count} generations. Blank circles mark people whose names were lost.
facts: The tree records {n} names collected from parish registers, oral histories and court files in {place}.
Writing it took the artist {months} weeks on a ladder.
process: The chalk is not fixed; visitors' sleeves slowly smudge the lower names.
quotes: Everyone in this room is related to everyone else. That is the problem and the answer.
turns: The tree is so large that the visitor can only ever stand inside it, never in front of it.
archetypes.camera: wide view of the dark room covered in white chalk writing

scenes.t: An altar crowded with candles, family photographs, plastic flowers, {m2} and a small CRT monitor playing home videos stands against the wall.
Columns hung with {m1}, fairy lights and tinsel stand in the nave like shrines.

facts: 0|Each object belonged to one of {n} friends the artist lost between {year_then} and now.
0|The altar was first assembled in the artist's flat in {place}.
1|The medicines were collected from {count} households in {place}.
process: 0|The candles are lit each morning and replaced when they burn down.
0|Visitors have begun to leave their own objects; they are kept.
1|The lights are switched on at dusk by the guards.
quotes: I keep things because nobody else did.
An altar is just a shelf that someone loves.
turns: 0|Hoarding becomes a form of care, and the shelf a place where the dead are still allowed to be particular.
1|Medicine becomes devotion, and the pharmacy a kind of church.
archetypes.camera: frontal view of the altar, warm candle light mixed with gallery light

scenes: A full-size replica of a chimney, built in {m1}, stands alone in the room; it is the only part of the artist's family house that survived.
A {m1} copy of a front door, frame and step from a demolished house in {place} stands on the floor, opening onto nothing.
facts: The house stood in {place} from {year_then} until it was destroyed last year.
The measurements were taken from {count} family photographs.
process: The structure was built by a bricklayer who had worked on the original house.
It is lit only by daylight.
quotes: It is the part of the house that was meant to keep us warm.
I rebuilt it so I could stop looking for it.
turns: Made transparent, the most solid part of a home becomes the most fragile thing in the room.
archetypes.camera: frontal view in daylight, the structure alone in the space

scenes.t: Hundreds of {m1} candles hang in dense clusters along the walls of a dim room. A woman sits at a table dipping wicks in hot wax, and the air is heavy with smoke.
A dome built from {count} plastic jerrycans, their spouts pointing down, stands in the room. Visitors can step inside, where a faint smell of incense hangs.

facts: 0|The wax came from {n} beekeepers in the hills around {place}.
1|The jerrycans were bought second-hand at a fuel market in {place}.
process: 0|Candles are made on site throughout the exhibition.
1|The structure was assembled without screws, held by weight alone.
quotes: 0|Light has to be made every day, like bread.
1|These cans carried petrol. Now they carry prayers.
turns: The work smells before it is seen, and the smell stays on the visitor's clothes after they leave.
archetypes.camera: view into the dim room with candles, smoky air

scenes.t: {count_word} {m1} figures walk in procession across the hall, carrying floral wreaths and vintage serving trays.
Bronze women with the heads and wings of birds stand around a glowing tree of {m2}, some holding weapons, others gifts.

facts: The figures were cast from {n} people in {place}, chosen by lottery.
The procession is modelled on a funeral the artist attended in {year_then}.
process: 0|The bronzes were cast in a foundry in {place} and left unpolished.
quotes: A procession is grief that agrees to keep walking.
turns: 0|Fixed in bronze, a moment of collective movement becomes a permanent rehearsal.
1|The figures stand guard over a tree that gives off its own light, as if keeping a secret from the visitor.
archetypes.camera: long view along the procession in the hall

scenes.t: Glitter-covered casts of fragments of the artist's friends' bodies, hands, knees and backs, spiral upwards like a slow tornado.

facts: 0|The casts were taken from {n} friends during a single night in {place} in {year_then}.
process: The casts were made in one night and never retouched.
quotes: 0|Together we make one body that nobody owns.
turns: 0|The work proposes the group as the only body that can protect each of its parts.
archetypes.camera: three-quarter view under bright gallery light

basis: Taring Padi cardboard puppets, documenta fifteen

scenes.t: Huge figures assembled from {m1}, {m2} and discarded household objects reach towards the ceiling, part guardian, part carnival float.
{count_word} life-size cardboard puppets stand in a crowd near the entrance, painted with slogans and faces.

facts: The materials were gathered on the beaches near {place} after a hurricane in {year_then}.
The puppets were made in {count} workshops with schoolchildren.
process: Nothing was bought; everything was found within walking distance of the studio.
quotes: The storm gave me my materials. I am only giving them back a shape.
turns: Out of debris, the work builds guardians for a place that was told it had nothing left.
archetypes.camera: low angle up at the figures in a large hangar-like space

scenes: A reimagined equestrian monument in {m1}: the rider has been replaced by a seated woman with her back to the horse.
A row of tall columns in {m1} stands outside by the water; their capitals are portraits of neighbours from {place}.
facts: The original monument has stood in {place} since {year_then}.
The faces belong to {n} people who run shops on the artist's street.
process: The portraits were modelled from life over {months} months.
quotes: Monuments decide who is allowed to be looked up to.
turns: The work answers the monument in its own language, and changes only who is speaking.
archetypes.camera: outdoor view in flat daylight

scenes.t: A tall tower built of {m1} and {m2} stands in the courtyard with speakers fixed to it; its sound mixes with the noise of the street.
Twenty old radios stand together on low stools, each playing a different part of one composition at the same time.

facts: 1|The composition cites a radio broadcast made from {place} in {year_then}.
It was recorded with {n} musicians over {count} nights.
0|The tower was built by {n} fishermen from {place} in {hours} days.
process: The sound is spread across {count} channels so that no visitor hears the whole piece.
quotes: Radio was the first internet, and the first loudspeaker for the powerless.
turns: The work asks who is allowed to fill the air.
archetypes.camera: view from the ground, outdoors or in a courtyard

scenes.t: A maze of scaffolding pipes about fifty metres long carries an automated organ that pushes a slow lament through its pipes. At its centre, water pulses in a round pool.
Hunks of coal hang from the ceiling on cords and are swung by motors against hand-made leather drums; the bass vibrates through the floor.

facts: The music was composed with {n} musicians from {place}.
0|The organ plays a cycle that lasts {hours} hours without repeating.
1|The coal comes from a mine near {place} that closed in {year_then}.
process: 0|The pipes were tuned on site over {months} weeks.
1|The drums were made by hand and will split before the end of the exhibition.
quotes: Listening is a way of paying attention to someone who is not speaking to you.
turns: The work is heard long before it is understood, and understood mostly in the body.
archetypes.camera: long view through the scaffolding maze

scenes.t: Glass megaphones on steel stands play recordings of insects at night; a faint scent drifts through the darkened room.
Two large red shells hang in a round room lit red. Visitors stand between them to hear voices coming from the openings.

facts: 0|The recordings were made at night in a forest outside {place} over {n} nights.
0|{count} of the species recorded are now considered endangered.
1|The voices belong to {n} people from {place} who spoke on condition of anonymity.
process: 0|The scent was composed with a perfumer and is refreshed every morning.
1|Only two visitors are allowed inside at a time.
quotes: 0|I want people to stop saying 'I know that, next'.
1|A shell is a natural speaker. The sea has always been talking.
turns: Asked to listen rather than look, the visitor becomes the slowest thing in the room.
archetypes.camera: dim room, objects lit from above, dark walls

basis: The Walls Have Ears, documenta fifteen

scenes.t: Headphones hang on hooks along a bare wall, each playing a different person from {place} reading a list of things they left behind.
Listening posts line a pedestrian tunnel, each playing the testimony of someone waiting for asylum.

facts: The {count} testimonies were recorded in {place} between {year_then} and last year.
Each speaker chose which language to speak in.
process: The recordings are unedited.
quotes: I wanted voices without faces, so nobody could decide what they looked like.
turns: The work trusts the visitor with the most intimate thing an exhibition can hold: time spent listening to a stranger.
archetypes.camera: eye-level view of the wall of headphones, a bench in front

scenes.t: A tangle of multicoloured rope lies on the floor with found buoys hung over it; a rope cast in salt hangs from the pile.
Rows of {m1} are laid out in a grid; from each one tangled branches grow upward like a thicket.

facts: 0|The traps were bought from fishermen in a harbour near {place} that closed in {year_then}.
0|Salt was once traded for people along the same coast.
1|The desks came from {count} village schools around {place} that closed in {year_then}.
process: 0|The salt rope was cast in {count} sections and joined on site.
1|Each branch was cut from hedges on the edge of {place} and wedged into the desk by hand.
quotes: Things wash up. People wash up. We decide which ones to keep.
turns: 0|The salt dissolves very slowly in the humid air, so that the heaviest history in the room is also the most fragile.
1|The classroom becomes a thicket, and the lesson something that grows back without permission.
archetypes.camera: three-quarter view of the floor sculpture, no barriers

scenes.t: A whole room is draped in {m1} stitched together by hand; inside stands a forest of mended {m2} rescued from public institutions.
Second-hand clothes are bound tight into {count_word} bales and stacked into a walled enclosure. Inside, a monitor plays a video of a market.

facts: 0|The sacks were used to carry cocoa from {place} to ports in Europe; some still carry the stamps of traders.
0|The chairs were collected from {count} schools and courts that closed in {year_then}.
1|The bales were bought by weight at a second-hand clothes market in {place}, where {count} tonnes arrive every week.
process: 0|The sacks were sewn together by {n} women in {place}, who were paid by the metre.
0|Local carpenters repaired each chair before it was installed.
1|The bales were not opened; their contents are listed on a sheet by the door.
quotes: 0|A sack has carried more than any museum.
0|The chairs are empty so that a parliament can sit in them.
1|These are the clothes the rich world gives away so that it can buy more.
turns: The room is both a monument to labour and a place where people can sit down.
interaction: The room hosts talks and meetings during the exhibition.
archetypes.camera: wide view into the draped room, warm light through the sacks

basis: Dima Srouji and Piero Tomassoni, Kochi 2025

scenes.t: Hundreds of {m1} hang on near-invisible wire over the heads of visitors, as if about to fall.
A tornado of detritus, newspaper, flags, tape and plastic, swirls on a circular screen mounted in the ceiling.

facts: 0|The {count} pieces were blown in two workshops, one in {place} and one across a border the artist cannot cross.
0|Each object was donated by a resident of {place}.
1|The footage was filmed from a rooftop in {place} during a storm in {year_then}.
process: Hanging the work took {n} technicians {hours} days.
1|The loop lasts {minutes} minutes and has no beginning.
quotes: I wanted the room to feel like the moment before something breaks.

basis: Chaw Ei Thein, Artists' Street, Berlin Biennale 13
Britto Arts Trust, Rasad, documenta fifteen
scenes: A street of small, soft, hand-stitched buildings and figures runs along a low platform; each scene shows a protest that took place in {place}.
facts: The scenes follow protests in {place} from {year_then} to the present.
process: Each figure was stitched while the artist was in exile.
quotes: You can make a street soft when you cannot make it safe.
turns: Rendered soft and small, political violence becomes something that can be held, and so remembered.
archetypes.camera: low view along the soft street

basis: Jenna Sutela, Aeolian Suite, Finnish Pavilion 2026

scenes.t: {count_word} sculptures stand in a circle like a wind rose, each covered in long fuzzy wigs like microphone wind covers; they turn and sing as the winds.
In a dim room, {count_word} soft silicone forms sit on shelves; metal rods prod them in rhythm, and they dent, swell and make sound.

facts: 0|The score follows the winds recorded at {place} over {n} days.
1|The forms were modelled on scans of the artist's own body.
process: The sculptures are controlled by a computer that never repeats a sequence.
quotes: 0|I wanted the weather to have a voice.
1|I wanted to hear what it sounds like when a thought is touched.
turns: 0|The work makes the invisible movement of air into a choir.
1|The soft forms make listening feel like a bodily act.

basis: Ei Arakawa-Nash, Grass Babies, Moon Babies, Venice 2026
scenes: Hundreds of heavy baby dolls in reflective sunglasses crawl across the floor, climb scaffolding and hang from ropes. Visitors may pick one up and carry it through the building.
facts: There are {count} dolls, weighted to the weight of a newborn.
process: Each evening the dolls are collected and returned to the room.
quotes: Care is heavy. I wanted people to feel the weight.
interaction: Visitors may carry a doll through the exhibition.
turns: The work turns the visitor into a carer for the length of a visit.
archetypes.camera: room full of dolls on floor and scaffolding

scenes: A gravel courtyard is cut in two by a narrow water channel. On one side about a hundred olive and citrus trees stand in red barrels on pallets; on the other, a red pallet jack rests on a marble block.
facts: The trees will be planted in {place} when the exhibition closes.
Each tree was paid for by a donor, whose name is kept in a ledger.
process: The trees are watered by hand every evening.
quotes: A tree in a barrel is a tree that is waiting to go home.
turns: Mobile and rooted at once, the trees are an orchard in transit.
archetypes.camera: courtyard with rows of trees in red barrels
